product.olivetti-m290s.summary: The compact office 286 combining integrated VGA, three expansion slots and drives for both floppy sizes.
product.olivetti-m290s.history: The Museo del Calcolatore dates the M290S to 1989. Italian advertising in June 1990 already offered it as a compact 16 MHz 286; the brochure preserved by VintAds presented it as the new starting point of Olivetti’s professional office and business range. Its configuration aimed to support work with MS-DOS, OS/2 and XENIX V/286, and exchange of 3.5- and 5.25-inch floppies in mixed installations. Sources: Museo del Calcolatore, M290S record; M290S brochure and Informatica telematica e scuola advertisement, June 1990, on VintAds.
product.olivetti-m290s.warning: Experimental 16 MHz, 1 MiB M203 profile. Both BIOS 1.29 ROMs are required. IDE options create a blank disk. Use F3 in the original Setup to select the matching type.
product.olivetti-m290s.technical.identit: Published clock speeds differ between sources. Olivetti’s brochure and advertisement specify 16 MHz; the Museo del Calcolatore lists 12 MHz. PC Rebuilding identifies the M203 board with an AMD N80L286-16/S. The 12 MHz figure has not been established as a separate commercial variant.
product.olivetti-m290s.technical.memory: RAM expansion let the machine adapt to its workload. PC Rebuilding describes 1 MB soldered down and four 30-pin SIMMs allowing 5 MB on the board. The brochure advertises 17 MB in the system; this is not a verified amount of addressable or usable memory.
product.olivetti-m290s.technical.board: Integrated video and connections left slots available for expansion. The Retro Web and the M203 photograph identify TACT82301/302/303 and Paradise PVGA1A, with VGA, serial, parallel and two PS/2 ports; the three 16-bit ISA slots require the riser card. Power uses a ten-pin Olivetti connector.
product.olivetti-m290s.technical.storage: Olivetti offered 20, 40 and 100 MB hard disks and 1.44 or 1.2 MB floppy drives. The original tutorial points to the onboard 40-pin hard disk connector. The BIOS uses PC/AT hard disk registers.
product.olivetti-m290s.technical.jumpers: Jumpers change functions that future emulation must respect. The manual, p. 3-5, assigns P1 to password, P2/P13 to parity and P4 to the CMOS battery; P3 selects ROM address E0000h by default or C0000h. The fragment does not resolve the entire memory map.
product.olivetti-m290s.technical.firmwar: The preserved files identify a revision but do not certify a successful boot. HIGH and LOW are each 64 KiB and their hashes match MAME olim203. Interleaving them in memory, LOW even and HIGH odd, reveals “Version 1.29” at 0x1E02B; the date string is “05/03/90”, with its order left uninterpreted.
product.olivetti-m290s.technical.verifie: The original Setup saved the 1.44 MB floppy drive and all three hard disk types. Olivetti MS-DOS 5.00 cold-booted from floppy and from each compatible IDE disk. C/H/S geometries: 615/4/17, 981/5/17 and 755/16/17.
product.olivetti-m290s.technical.limitat: BluMach uses a compatible IDE controller. The M203 pinout and exact logic remain unconfirmed. The profile reuses the PCS 286/S TACT memory approximation and PC87310. RAM expansion and other board revisions remain untested.
product.olivetti-m290s.technical.source_: VintAds, Olivetti M290S brochure dated 1990 by the archive: positioning and expansion. The transcription page and preview are preserved; the full TIFF requires access and has not been acquired.

VintAds, Olivetti M290S advertisement in Informatica telematica e scuola, June 1990: 16 MHz, compatibility and mixed floppy drives. Page and preview preserved; advertising superlatives are not adopted as facts.
Olivetti, M290S General Service Manual, 0201730V: nine-page fragment including 1-23 and 3-4/3-5. Copy of the minuszerodegrees archive preserved from the Stuttgart mirror.
Museo del Calcolatore “Laura Tellini”, M290S: 1989 date and 12 MHz CPU. This discrepancy with the advertised 16 MHz is retained.
PC Rebuilding, “Olivetti M203 (M290S) 286”: board, CPU and RAM identification. Collection evidence does not establish every product revision.

The Retro Web, M203: components and photograph by dataino.it, CC BY-SA 4.0, unchanged. The image filename contains “m320”; the M203 attribution comes from the record and cross-checking, not that filename.
MAME fc81fbe1, src/mame/pc/at.cpp: olim203, LOW/HIGH layout, hashes and MACHINE_NOT_WORKING. It does not establish compatibility with M290 or M290 SP.
